quota_rule: No per-batch ceiling (plan/25-content-commissions.md K-005, Roy 09/09; reconfirmed 12/09 — spotCheckPlan() is now called per batch file, scripts/build-ingest-sql.mjs:159, not over the whole bank, so the 1,200-row ceiling is a per-FILE bound, not a per-tick quota). Batch size = 30, chosen as a deliberate, measured step up from the 12-word batches this queue had settled into out of an over-read of the old whole-bank ceiling: 30 is what could still be individually written, checked against data/generated/allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt for every non-target token via a real gateSense run (not a sample), and manually reviewed sentence-by-sentence for translation accuracy within this tick, without lowering the per-item bar the gate and R-013/R-014 hold. The real bottleneck this tick was per-item human care (Hebrew translation precision, distractor testing in the actual stems, allowed-words compliance of every example/item sentence), not the technical pipeline, which the previous batches' manifests already show runs clean well past 30 rows per file.
note: R-014 (replaced 10/09): no human sample-review queue; 23/30 rows carry translation_confidence = 'high', 7/30 (boiled, bonus, bookcase, bookshelf, brainstorm, breeze, camping) carry 'medium' because the single Hebrew word or short phrase chosen only approximately covers the English sense (e.g. 'boiled' vs the broader 'מבושל' also used for 'cooked'; 'camping' where קמפינג/מחנאות are both live in Hebrew usage) — flagged rather than asserted, per policy. gateSense (lib/core/contentSchema.ts) ran directly against all 30 rows before writing, via a scratch validator script (.scratch/checkgate.mjs, not committed) that imports the real gateSense and the real data/generated/allowed-words-2026-08-07.txt: first pass was 15/30 (15 rows failed on level drift — a spelled-out day/month/number or an everyday noun such as 'potatoes', 'fork', 'noon', 'buildings' not present in the NGSL-derived allowed-words surface-form list); every failure was rewritten with an allowed-words-checked substitute and a second pass ran 30/30 clean. Two distractor-shape bugs caught by the same script before the gate run: 'camping' and 'carrot' each originally listed themselves as their own 'orthographic' distractor (would have failed as 'is the headword'), and four rows (bride, cab, cassette, chef) used a 'near_synonym' distractor as one of only four distractors, leaving 3 scorable instead of the required 4 — both classes of bug were fixed before the gate run, not discovered by it. A 7-item negative control (one deliberately broken row per failure mode: level drift, leaked answer, Latin letters in translation, fewer than 4 scorable distractors, missing blank, nikud in translation, headword missing from example), built on a passing row from this batch, ran through the same real gate: 0/7 passed, confirming the gate still discriminates. ⚠️ OPEN FINDING, reported rather than worked around: the informal 'set-diff distractors against allowed-words' practice in plan/80-content-lessons.md § א׳1 (rows on C-0164/C-0350) was written for the earlier era when both headwords AND distractors were drawn from the same NGSL v1.2 list; a manual check of this batch's 4x30=120 distractor words against that same list found 51/120 absent (e.g. 'banana', 'umbrella', 'insect', 'unhappy', 'diary' — ordinary A1/A2 words, not level drift). gateSense itself does not check distractor words against allowedWords at all (confirmed by reading lib/core/contentSchema.ts directly) — the practice was always a CONTENT-side discipline layered on top of the machine gate, not the gate itself, and it does not fit the current sourcing model where headwords come from the CEFR-J-derived data/amirnet-vocab.csv rather than NGSL. Distractors were kept to simple, common, A1/A2-level English words by manual judgment; none was force-fitted into the older 2,818-lemma NGSL list, since doing so would mean picking worse (rarer, less natural) distractors to satisfy a reference list built for a different word source. Recommend PM/DEV decide whether a fresh allowed-words list should be derived from data/amirnet-vocab.csv (or CEFR-J itself) for distractor-level checking going forward; flagged here rather than decided unilaterally. npm run build:ingest ran cleanly afterward over the full bank — see the commit for the exact row/file counts and the ISO 2859-1 basis, which the pre-push gate re-verifies. npm run measure:gate, npm run build:levels and npm run build:preview all ran clean. No number is written as a word above 'one' and no proper name appears in any example or item stem (checked by script, not by eye).
